      #!/bin/bash
      #SBATCH --job-name=proj_002_s0_init
      #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6
      #SBATCH --mem=85G
      #SBATCH --output=<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s0_init_%j.out
      #SBATCH --error=<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s0_init_%j.err
      #
      # Generated by swereg::tteplan_export_slurm(). Do not edit.
      # spec version: v003
      # stage 1 of 5: s0_init (script s0_init.R)
      # progress denominators: 123456 ids across 4 skeleton files
      #
      # The driver script submits this file. This file submits nothing.
      
      set -euo pipefail
      
      swereg_dir_tteplan='<DIR_TTEPLAN>'
      swereg_touch_path='<DIR_TTEPLAN>/tteplan.qs2'
      swereg_expect_fstype='<FSTYPE>'
      swereg_repo='<DIR_REPO>'
      swereg_stage_script='<DIR_REPO>/s0_init.R'
      swereg_mem_log='<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s0_init_mem.log'
      
      # Mount check. Read a path under the data directory before you read the
      # filesystem type. An automounted share stays unmounted until something
      # reads a path under it, and a type read on an unmounted automount
      # reports the local disk. That order fails a healthy job.
      head -c 1 -- "$swereg_touch_path" > /dev/null
      swereg_fstype="$(stat -f -c %T -- "$swereg_dir_tteplan")"
      if [ "$swereg_fstype" != "$swereg_expect_fstype" ]; then
        printf 'swereg: %s is on filesystem %s, expected %s\n' \
          "$swereg_dir_tteplan" "$swereg_fstype" "$swereg_expect_fstype" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      
      # Peak memory, written on every exit. The scheduler's own accounting is
      # empty on some builds, so this job reads the kernel counter itself.
      swereg_record_peak_memory() {
        if [ -r /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak ]; then
          printf 'memory_peak_bytes %s\n' \
            "$(cat -- /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak)" > "$swereg_mem_log"
        elif [ -r /proc/self/status ]; then
          printf 'vmhwm_kb %s\n' \
            "$(awk -- '/^VmHWM:/ { print $2 }' /proc/self/status)" \
            > "$swereg_mem_log"
        else
          printf 'peak_memory_unavailable\n' > "$swereg_mem_log"
        fi
      }
      trap swereg_record_peak_memory EXIT
      
      # The plan on disk MUST carry the schema version this swereg understands.
      # The path after the expression takes no `--` terminator: Rscript passes
      # `--` through as the argument itself. The path is absolute instead.
      Rscript -e 'swereg::tteplan_locate_and_load(commandArgs(TRUE)[1])$check_version()' "$swereg_dir_tteplan"
      
      cd -- "$swereg_repo"
      Rscript "$swereg_stage_script"

      #!/bin/bash
      #
      # Generated by swereg::tteplan_export_slurm(). Do not edit.
      # spec version: v003
      # project: proj_002
      # 5 stages: s0_init, s1, s2, s3, s4_export
      #
      # Submits one job per stage. Each dependant starts only after the stage
      # before it finishes with exit code 0.
      
      set -euo pipefail
      
      # Slurm records the submitting directory as each job's working directory.
      cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")"
      
      swereg_jid_01="$(sbatch --parsable -- '<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s0_init.sh')"
      printf 'submitted %s as %s\n' 's0_init' "$swereg_jid_01"
      
      swereg_jid_02="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:"$swereg_jid_01" --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes --no-requeue -- '<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s1.sh')"
      printf 'submitted %s as %s\n' 's1' "$swereg_jid_02"
      
      swereg_jid_03="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:"$swereg_jid_02" --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes -- '<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s2.sh')"
      printf 'submitted %s as %s\n' 's2' "$swereg_jid_03"
      
      swereg_jid_04="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:"$swereg_jid_03" --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes -- '<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s3.sh')"
      printf 'submitted %s as %s\n' 's3' "$swereg_jid_04"
      
      swereg_jid_05="$(sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:"$swereg_jid_04" --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes -- '<DIR_OUT>/slurm/proj_002_s4_export.sh')"
      printf 'submitted %s as %s\n' 's4_export' "$swereg_jid_05"
